items.title: Povorcitinib for nonsegmental vitiligo: two randomized, controlled, phase 3 STOP-V trials.
items.abstract: There is an unmet need for repigmentation therapies for patients with nonsegmental vitiligo (NSV) who are candidates for systemic therapy. Here, 52-week primary results are reported from two parallel phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of once-daily povorcitinib (oral, highly selective JAK1 inhibitor) 30 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe NSV (STOP-V1 and STOP-V2). STOP-V1 and STOP-V2 enrolled 467 and 449 patients, respectively. In both studies, the primary endpoint of ≥75% improvement in the facial Vitiligo Area Scoring Index (F-VASI75) at week 52 was met, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful repigmentation with povorcitinib versus placebo (STOP-V1: 18.9% versus 6.8%; odds ratio, 3.1; 95% confidence interval 1.6-5.9; P = 0.0003; STOP-V2: 18.9% versus 3.1%; odds ratio, 7.5; 95% confidence interval 3.0-18.6; P < 0.0001). Povorcitinib was well tolerated; the percentage of patients with any treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) was similar between the povorcitinib and placebo groups in both studies (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 68.7%/66.7% versus 63.7%/62.7%). The most common TEAEs with povorcitinib were nasopharyngitis (STOP-V1/STOP-V2, 11.2%/11.3% versus placebo, 9.8%/11.1%), acne (10.7%/10.8% versus 3.0%/2.2%) and upper respiratory tract infection (6.9%/14.0% versus 9.0%/10.7%). Serious TEAEs were generally single events, and Janus kinase inhibitor class-specific TEAEs were absent or rare. These results support once-daily povorcitinib as an effective and well-tolerated systemic treatment for adults with moderate-to-severe NSV. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers: NCT06113445 , NCT06113471 .

items.title: Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20-CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma.
METHODS: DALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866).
FINDINGS: Between Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; p<0·0001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 63 (83%) of 76 with zamto-cel and in 65 (86%) of 76 with R-GemOx. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (28 [37%] with zamto-cel and 17 [22%] with R-GemOx), anaemia (11 [14%] and 12 [16%]), and decreased neutrophil count (20 [26%] and seven [9%]). Serious adverse events occurred in 31 (41%) patients with zamto-cel and 50 (66%) with R-GemOx, most commonly malignant neoplasm progression (11 [14%] and 38 [50%]), cytokine release syndrome (CRS; six [8%] and none), and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (four [5%] and none). Treatment-related deaths occurred in two (3%) of 82 patients with zamto-cel (due to CRS and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis) and in one (1%) of 78 with R-GemOx (malignant lymphoma progression).
INTERPRETATION: The risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.

BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.
METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.
RESULTS: A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

items.title: Coronary CT Angiography versus Intravascular Ultrasound Guidance for PCI.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)-guided percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) improves clinical outcomes. Coronary computed tomographic angiography (CCTA) provides anatomical and physiological information before cardiac catheterization that may enable PCI planning. Data regarding the use of CCTA-guided PCI as compared with IVUS-guided PCI with respect to clinical outcomes are lacking.
METHODS: In this investigator-initiated, international, open-label, randomized, noninferiority trial with blinded end-point adjudication, we randomly assigned patients with a clinical indication for revascularization, at least one epicardial lesion with a diameter stenosis of more than 70%, and a fractional flow reserve derived from CCTA of 0.80 or less in a 1:1 ratio to a CCTA-guided or IVUS-guided PCI strategy. The primary end point was target-vessel failure, defined as a composite of death from cardiac causes, target-vessel myocardial infarction, or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization, at 12 months. The noninferiority margin for the absolute risk difference was 4.5 percentage points, with a prespecified hierarchical testing strategy for superiority.
RESULTS: A total of 1105 patients underwent randomization: 556 to the CCTA-guided PCI group and 549 to the IVUS-guided PCI group. The median age of the patients was 65 years, and 21.7% were women. At 12 months, target-vessel failure had occurred in 23 patients (4.1%) in the CCTA-guided PCI group and in 25 patients (4.6%) in the IVUS-guided PCI group (risk difference, -0.42 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -2.82 to 1.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.73 for superiority). A total of 6 patients in the CCTA-guided PCI group and 9 patients in the IVUS-guided PCI group had clinical procedural complications.
CONCLUSIONS: A CCTA-guided PCI strategy was noninferior to IVUS-guided PCI with respect to target-vessel failure at 12 months. (Funded by GE HealthCare and Heartflow; P4 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05253677.).

items.title: Tenecteplase Before Thrombectomy at 4.5 to 24 Hours for Basilar Artery Occlusion: The ATTENTION LATE Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Whether intravenous tenecteplase before endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) improves outcomes in patients with basilar artery occlusion presenting 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous tenecteplase before EVT vs EVT alone in patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion admitted within 4.5 to 24 hours from stroke onset.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, open-label, blinded end point, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 40 stroke centers in China. Between March 16, 2023, and February 4, 2025, a total of 330 patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≥10) presenting within 4.5 to 24 hours from stroke onset to EVT-capable centers were enrolled. Final follow-up was completed on May 4, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized 1:1 via a centralized web server using a minimization method to receive either intravenous tenecteplase (bolus injection, 0.25 mg/kg; maximum, 25 mg) followed by EVT (n = 166) or EVT alone (n = 164).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality.
RESULTS: Among 332 patients randomized, 2 withdrew consent. Of the remaining 330 patients (mean [SD] age, 66 [11] years; 241 males [73%]; 89 females [27%]), 329 completed 90-day follow-up. Of whom, 50 of 165 (30%) in the tenecteplase plus EVT group and 50 of 164 (30%) in the EVT alone group achieved functional independence (adjusted rate ratio, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.67 to 1.25]; risk difference, -0.18% [95% CI, -10.13% to 9.76%]). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 8 patients (5%) in the tenecteplase plus EVT group and 6 (4%) in the EVT alone group. Mortality at 90 days was similar between the groups (66 [40%] vs 70 [43%], respectively).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with moderate to severe basilar artery occlusion admitted directly to EVT-capable centers who presented 4.5 to 24 hours after stroke onset, the addition of intravenous tenecteplase before EVT did not result in improved functional outcomes compared with EVT alone.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05701956.

items.title: Digital Outreach to Improve Statin Refills in Patients With Low Statin Adherence: The ADHERE-ASCVD Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Statin nonadherence is a leading, addressable driver of preventable cardiovascular events. Although health systems routinely use outreach to promote preventive care, most strategies are static and lack evidence from randomized clinical trials.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an adaptive, sequential digital outreach strategy improves short-term statin refill vs usual communication among adults with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) or high ASCVD risk and recent nonadherence within a rapidly implemented, health system-embedded randomized clinical trial.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Pragmatic, health system-embedded, prospective randomized open blinded end point (PROBE) clinical trial using a 2-stage sequential, multiple assignment, randomized trial (SMART) design. The trial was conducted via Kaiser Permanente Northern California, an integrated health care delivery system serving more than 4.6 million members. Eligible participants were adults 18 years or older with established ASCVD or high ASCVD risk, recent statin nonadherence, and eligibility for all study communication modalities.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive secure portal messaging, SMS/text messaging, nonsecure email, or usual communication. Initial nonresponders within 14 days underwent prespecified second-stage randomization to repeat the same outreach, switch communication modality, or receive usual communication.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Rates of 14-day statin refill following each randomization, with 28-day follow-up.
RESULTS: Among 20 604 participants (mean [SD] age, 54.8 [9.0] years; 40.9% female; 27.8% Asian, 10.9% Black, 33.6% Hispanic; 15.3% with established ASCVD), initial digital outreach increased 14-day statin refill vs usual communication (14.4% vs 12.0%; adjusted risk difference, 2.3 percentage points [95% CI, 1.3-3.4]; adjusted risk ratio, 1.20 [95% CI, 1.10-1.30]). Among initial nonresponders, second-stage outreach further increased refill (13.0% vs 10.4%; adjusted risk difference, 2.5 percentage points [95% CI, 1.3-3.7]; adjusted risk ratio, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.11-1.39]). Switching communication modalities did not improve refill vs repeating the same modality (13.2% vs 12.5%; adjusted risk ratio, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.94-1.17]). Cumulative statin refill through 28 days was higher in those receiving any digital outreach vs usual communication (24.9% vs 21.2%; adjusted hazard ratio, 1.21 [95% CI, 1.13-1.30]). Results were consistent across prespecified subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adults with a statin indication and recent statin nonadherence, adaptive outreach improved short-term refill vs usual communication. A second outreach produced additional gains among initial nonresponders, although switching communication modalities provided no additional benefit. These findings support adaptive, sequential health system outreach strategies to improve cardiovascular prevention when integrated into population health programs.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07522645.

items.title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial.
items.abstract: Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0-23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8-100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05845450 .

items.title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

items.title: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccination in Pregnancy and Child Neurodevelopment at 18 to 30 Months.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Little is known about neurodevelopmental outcomes of children exposed to SARS-CoV-2 messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine during pregnancy. Evidence on long-term offspring outcomes after in utero exposure to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination is needed to inform vaccine recommendations in pregnancy.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether there is an association between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or shortly before pregnancy and offspring neurodevelopmental measures.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, prospective, cohort study of 18- to 30-month-old children was conducted at 14 centers of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network from 2024 through 2025. Women who received a SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine during or within 30 days prior to pregnancy (exposed) were matched with women who did not (unexposed) by delivery site, delivery date, insurance status, and race and ethnicity. These data were analyzed from June 2025 to May 2026.
EXPOSURES: Maternal receipt of at least 1 dose of an mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccine during, or within 30 days prior to, the index pregnancy vs no SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during pregnancy or within 30 days prior.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was Ages and Stages Questionnaire version 3 (ASQ-3) total score, which was deemed to be equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups if the 90% CI of the median difference was between -10 and 10. Secondary outcomes included domain-specific ASQ-3 scores, the Child Behavior Checklist, Modified Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, and Early Childhood Behavior Questionnaire scores.
RESULTS: Of 3956 screened, 271 exposed and 240 unexposed children were enrolled. Matching on all characteristics was possible in 217 pairs. Of the 434 children enrolled, 258 (59.4%) were Non-Hispanic White, 96 (22.1%) Non-Hispanic Black, 52 (12.0%) Hispanic, and 28 (6.5%) were not represented by any of the above racial or ethnic groups. Median age at assessment was 25.8 [24.6 to 28.3] months, 221 were female (50.9%), and 213 were male (49.1%). Exposed mothers were more likely to be nulliparous; their children were slightly younger at assessment and more likely to have been vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. The primary outcome of ASQ-3 score was equivalent between the exposed and unexposed groups (255 vs 260, adjusted median difference, -3.4; 90% CI, -9.8 to 3.0). There were no significant differences in secondary outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this multicenter cohort study, ASQ-3 scores were equivalent between 18- to 30-month-old children whose mothers did or did not receive mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccination during or immediately prior to pregnancy. These findings support continued recommendations for SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy.

items.title: Decompression With or Without Fusion Across Subgroups With Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis : A Target Trial Emulation.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States.
OBJECTIVE: To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups.
DESIGN: Cohort study using the target trial framework.
SETTING: Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial.
PATIENTS: Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months.
INTERVENTION: Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone.

items.title: Delirium and Long-Term Cognitive Trajectories in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Delirium is a state of acute confusion characterized by deficits in attention that occurs commonly during hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes; however, the association of delirium with longitudinal cognitive trajectories is not fully understood.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association of delirium during hospitalization with subsequent development of mild cognitive impairment (MCI), dementia, and longitudinal cognitive trajectories.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used data from participants with hospitalizations in the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) from October 2004 to December 2023. The MCSA is a prospective, population-based longitudinal study of cognitive aging among residents of Olmsted County, Minnesota. Of participants enrolled in the MCSA between 2004 and 2023, individuals who experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter were included in this study. Participants with dementia at MCSA enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. Follow-up continued until development of MCI or dementia, last MCSA visit, or the end of the study.
EXPOSURE: Delirium was identified using a validated natural language processing algorithm applied to clinical notes from hospitalizations, associated emergency department visits, and follow-up within 30 days after hospitalization. Delirium status was modeled as a time-dependent exposure.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Incident MCI and dementia were assigned through MCSA expert consensus evaluations, including neuropsychological testing performed every 15 months. Association between delirium and development of MCI or dementia was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for patient age, sex, level of education, and apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele carrier status; cognitive trajectories were assessed with linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: Of 7030 participants enrolled in the MCSA, 3542 individuals experienced 1 or more hospitalization prior to their last MCSA encounter and were included, and 41 participants with dementia at enrollment or prior to first hospitalization were excluded. The cohort included 3501 participants with at least 1 hospitalization. Median (IQR) age was 74.1 (66.6-80.9) years, 1676 participants (47.9%) were female, median (IQR) level of education was 14 (12-16) years, and 910 participants (26.0%) were APOE ε4 carriers. During a median (IQR) follow-up of 7.2 (4.1-10.4) years, 75 participants (2.1%) had delirium documented within 30 days of hospitalization. Delirium was associated with increased risk of MCI (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 3.67; 95% CI, 2.19-6.15) and dementia (aHR, 5.39; 95% CI, 2.94-9.85) and with accelerated decline in longitudinal cognitive testing.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study among adults in the MCSA, including those with unimpaired cognition at baseline, delirium during hospitalization was strongly associated with increased risk of MCI and dementia and accelerated cognitive decline in subsequent years.

items.title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is highly prevalent in patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) is a novel index to assess CMD independently of epicardial disease and driving pressures, but the long-term prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR in patients with ANOCA is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic value of continuous thermodilution-derived MRR and its association with clinical outcomes and symptom burden in patients with ANOCA.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This prospective, multicenter cohort study within the Netherlands Registry of Invasive Coronary Vasomotor Function Testing (NL-CFT) included patients between July 2020 and June 2025 in 4 clinical centers in the Netherlands. Follow-up for clinical events and patient-reported symptoms was completed for up to 3 years. Clinical events were adjudicated by investigators blinded to CFT results. Consecutive patients with ANOCA who underwent continuous thermodilution were included.
EXPOSURE: Abnormal MRR (CMD) was defined as less than 2.1, gray zone as 2.1 to 2.7, and normal microvascular function as 2.7 or greater.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was a composite of all-cause death, acute coronary syndrome, stroke, clinically indicated revascularization, repeat angiography without intervention, and unplanned hospital admittance or emergency department visit due to angina or heart failure. Secondary outcomes included angina at baseline and follow-up. Symptoms were assessed using the patient-reported Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) scores.
RESULTS: Among 553 included patients (mean [SD] age, 59.1 [9.6] years; 459 female [83.0%]) with a mean (SD) follow-up of 27.5 (16.1) months, CMD was observed in 94 patients (17.0%). The main composite outcome did not differ across the 3 MRR categories (18 of 94 patients with abnormal [19.1%] vs 21 of 98 patients with gray zone [21.4%] vs 76 of 361 patients with normal [21.1%] MRR; log-rank P = .85). Individual outcomes did not differ between groups. There was no overall longitudinal interaction between MRR and SAQ summary scores. While low MRR (abnormal vs normal groups) was not associated with an increased symptom burden at baseline, it was associated with worse angina at follow-up (mean [SD] SAQ summary score, 53.0 [16.7] vs 60.1 [16.6]; P = .04) and less clinically relevant improvement (9 of 30 patients [30.0%] vs 52 of 88 patients [59.1%]; P = .02).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, CMD assessed by continuous thermodilution-derived MRR was not associated with clinical outcomes.

items.title: Sodium bicarbonate therapy for metabolic acidosis in critically ill patients: a Bayesian systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
items.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of sodium bicarbonate therapy on mortality and renal outcomes in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis.
METHODS: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 2025, with an updated search on 2 April 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation, 90-day mortality, RRT-free days, vasopressor-free days, intensive care unit and hospital length of stay and adverse events.
RESULTS: Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified.
CONCLUSION: Current randomised evidence does not demonstrate a clear survival benefit from sodium bicarbonate therapy in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, but suggests a high probability of reducing RRT initiation. Further trials should define the patients most likely to benefit. PROSPERO registration: CRD420251246519.

items.abstract:
Nature Medicine, Published online: 03 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04686-y

In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo and resulted in fewer bloodstream infections, indicating further clinical investigation of this therapeutic is warranted.
